nutshell: An AI-fueled rebound continues amid lingering tariff concerns.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: This is the market closing brief for February 25th. It looks like the market managed to bounce back today after yesterday's big drop.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. Today's market can be summed up as an AI-fueled rebound amid persistent tariff worries. The S&P 500 gained 0.77% to close at 6,890.07, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.04% to 22,863.68. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also rose 0.76%, finishing the day at 49,174.50. Despite President Trump's new 10% tariffs taking effect today, the market shook off yesterday's losses. Positive news from the AI sector, in particular, revived investor sentiment and led the tech-driven rally.

sources.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq climb after AI-fueled sell-off as new Trump tariff kicks in

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: It's interesting that the market rallied even as that tariff headwind became a reality. What was the news out of the AI space?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Well, yesterday the market was weighed down by concerns that technology from AI startup Anthropic could threaten established software companies. But the situation completely turned around today when Anthropic announced several new corporate partnerships. This news sparked a relief rally in software-related stocks that had been falling on fears of AI's disruptive power, and that became the catalyst for the broader market rebound. On top of that, growing anticipation for Nvidia's earnings report, scheduled for tomorrow, brought strong buying into tech stocks.

sources.title: US software stocks climb as Anthropic announcement sparks relief rally
Tech news today: Countdown to Nvidia earnings begins as AI fears weigh on stocks

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: I see. So, to wrap up, could you summarize the key drivers that moved the market today?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, there were two main takeaways from today's session. First, the market showed resilience even in the face of new tariffs. And second, it's clear that AI is now steering the market, acting sometimes as a source of fear and other times as a source of relief.

sources.title: President Trump State of the Union Speech

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Alright, let's start with that first point you mentioned: the tariffs. What was the reason the market was able to rally even as these new tariffs took effect?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: It was certainly a rollercoaster ride for the market. Last Monday, uncertainty over the new tariff policy sent the S&P 500 down over one percent, and the VIX index, known as the fear gauge, spiked above 22 intraday, its highest level this February. Investors flocked to the safety of government bonds, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield down to around 4.03 percent. The industrials and consumer discretionary sectors, which are highly dependent on imports, were hit particularly hard. However, the market managed to rebound yesterday, when the tariffs took effect, and again today during the State of the Union address. This is being seen as a combination of relief that the President didn't announce the worst-case scenario, like further tariff hikes, and the strength in AI-related stocks. That said, the Dollar Index is still hovering around the 97 level, suggesting that caution hasn't completely disappeared from the currency markets.

sources.title: Stock market today: Dow drops 800 points as S&P 500, Nasdaq slide on Trump tariff fears, AI 'scare trade'
Trump’s 10% Levy Takes Effect as US Rebuilds Tariff Wall

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: What specifically was said about tariffs in yesterday's State of the Union address that gave the market a sense of relief?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: In the address, the President strongly defended his tariff policy but didn't mention an immediate additional increase in rates, which was the market's biggest fear. This helped calm investor sentiment by signaling that the worst-case scenario had been avoided for now. However, the conflict is far from over. Skepticism about the policy exists even within the Republican party, and major trading partners like the European Union are warning that the new tariffs could violate existing trade agreements. Furthermore, polls show that 64 percent of Americans do not support the President's tariff policy, raising questions about whether the political momentum can be sustained.

sources.title: Trump prepares to make new case for tariffs at State of the Union. Even some Republicans are skeptical.
EU Warns That Trump’s New Tariff Policy Breaks Trade Agreement
Trump’s 10% Levy Takes Effect as US Rebuilds Tariff Wall
President Trump State of the Union Speech

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So, we've avoided the worst, but the uncertainty remains. What are the practical implications of this tariff policy for the U.S. economy and for corporations going forward?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Despite the short-term relief, the medium-to-long-term burdens are significant. The legal basis for these tariffs, Section 122 of the Trade Act, allows them to be maintained for only up to 150 days without congressional approval, meaning we'll face this policy uncertainty again at the end of July. Many economists argue that the administration's justification for the tariffs—a balance of payments crisis—doesn't hold up, leaving the door open for future legal challenges. In fact, major companies like FedEx are already suing for refunds on previous tariffs that were ruled unconstitutional by the Supreme Court, setting up a confrontation with the administration. Ultimately, the concern is that this tariff wall will increase costs for businesses, which will eventually be passed on to consumers as higher prices, potentially undermining the Fed's efforts to control inflation.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Right, so the market is relieved for now, but it seems this tariff issue could continue to be a drag on the market in the long run. Thanks for that detailed analysis.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Okay, and the other key driver for the market today was AI. Yesterday, it dragged the market down with fear, but today it sparked a relief rally. What was behind such a dramatic shift in sentiment in just one day?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, the market's mood on the single keyword of 'artificial intelligence' was night and day. While the S&P 500 successfully rebounded 0.77 percent and the Nasdaq 1.04 percent today, the journey was quite dramatic. What weighed on the market yesterday was the fear that AI could destroy existing industries—what's being called the 'AI scare trade.' But today, the very source of that fear, the AI startup Anthropic, showed the potential for collaboration rather than destruction by announcing new partnerships, leading to a rapid recovery in investor sentiment. During this process, the VIX, the market's volatility index, fell over 6 percent from the 21-level yesterday to the 19-level today, showing that fear was quickly subsiding. The 10-year Treasury yield also stabilized, reviving risk appetite. In the end, an intense psychological battle over AI completely reversed the market's direction in just 24 hours.

sources.title: Stock market today: Dow drops 800 points as S&P 500, Nasdaq slide on Trump tariff fears, AI 'scare trade'
US software stocks climb as Anthropic announcement sparks relief rally

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: You mentioned this 'AI fear'—what exactly was that? How was the technology from a startup like Anthropic threatening enough to pull down the entire market?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: The fear in the market yesterday started with new AI features unveiled by Anthropic. For example, when news broke that its AI could modernize a company's old COBOL programming language, IBM's stock plunged nearly 13 percent, its biggest drop since the year 2000. Similarly, when Anthropic demonstrated an AI that could find and fix software security vulnerabilities on its own, shares of cybersecurity firms like CrowdStrike and Datadog fell sharply. This wasn't just about specific companies; it spread to a structural concern that the business models of software giants like Adobe and Salesforce could be replaced by AI. Some even started using the term 'SaaS-pocalypse,' meaning the end of software-as-a-service, which fueled the sell-off.

sources.title: IBM Sinks Most Since 2000 as Anthropic Touts COBOL Modernization
CrowdStrike, Datadog and other cybersecurity stocks slide after Anthropic's AI tool launch
Investors Are Dumping Software Stocks and Earnings Won’t Stop It

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: But then, in just one day, that fear turned into relief. How did Anthropic's partnership announcement manage to calm those fears?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That was the key to today's market reversal. At an event today, Anthropic announced that it would offer its AI technology not as a replacement for existing companies, but as a plug-in to be integrated into their work environments. For instance, they laid out a vision of collaborating with companies like Salesforce's Slack, DocuSign, and FactSet to use AI to assist with specific tasks like investment analysis or HR management. This announcement created the perception that AI could be a collaborator and an assistant, not a destroyer, which brought a sense of relief that yesterday's fears were overblown. On this news, the software tech stocks that had plunged yesterday all rebounded strongly. In particular, companies mentioned as partners, like Thomson Reuters, saw their shares surge over 10 percent.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So the perception shifted from AI being a destroyer of existing industries to a potential new growth opportunity. In this context, Nvidia's earnings report tomorrow becomes even more critical.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Exactly. The volatility of the past two days has shown just how sensitive the market is to AI's potential, and now all eyes are on the earnings release from Nvidia, the bellwether of the AI industry. The market wants to see from Nvidia's results whether investment in AI infrastructure is still going strong. The key points to watch will be the revenue growth in its core data center division and its future guidance. The options market is pricing in a potential move of more than 6 percent for Nvidia's stock after the announcement, which suggests that its earnings will be a major factor in determining the direction not just for AI, but for the entire market.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Right, and while Nvidia's earnings will be a key indicator for the AI market, there was also some very hot action in individual stocks today. Specifically, Nvidia's competitor AMD saw its stock surge over 8 percent at the close on news of a massive supply deal with Meta. What's the significance of this deal?

sources.title: AMD Just Won Another Massive AI Chip Deal. Its Stock Is Soaring.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Yes, this deal is being seen as a game-changer that could fundamentally alter AMD's future growth trajectory. The market is interpreting this not just as a revenue boost, but as a seal of approval from an industry leader like Meta, validating AMD's technology. The prevailing analysis is that this could create a domino effect, accelerating the adoption of AMD chips by other major cloud companies that were concerned about their supply chain dependence on Nvidia. In effect, this deal seems to have solidified AMD's strategic position as the only viable alternative to Nvidia in the AI accelerator market.

sources.title: Facebook owner Meta to buy AI chips from AMD in deal worth up to $100 billion
Meta strikes up to $100B AMD chip deal as it chases ‘personal superintelligence’

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Being called the only alternative to Nvidia is quite impressive. But for a deal that could change a company's destiny like this, I imagine there must be significant hidden risks as well.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's a sharp observation. Some are even calling this deal a 'poisoned chalice.' The biggest concern is that two structural vulnerabilities, which AMD itself acknowledged in its 10-K filing, have been amplified by this contract. The first is 'dependence on a small number of customers.' Potentially, more than half of its annual revenue could now depend on Meta alone, making the entire company vulnerable to a single shift in Meta's strategy. The second is the 'supply chain dependency risk,' as it relies entirely on a single source, Taiwan's TSMC, for the production of its core products. This means the fulfillment of this massive contract depends on external factors beyond AMD's control.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So it's facing two huge risks: a single customer and a single supply chain. But isn't the fact that Meta received warrants to acquire a stake in AMD also seen as evidence of a strong partnership?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's the central debate around this deal. Viewed positively, it's a strategic alliance. But from a critical perspective, it's seen as definitive proof of AMD's weaker negotiating position. These warrants represent a potential cost that could dilute the value for existing shareholders by up to 10 percent. Its competitor, Nvidia, is known to secure deals without such incentives, which could suggest that AMD had to put future shareholder value on the table to win the contract because its product competitiveness alone wasn't enough. Therefore, it might be more realistic to view this not just as strengthening a partnership, but as the price AMD had to pay to get the deal done.

sources.title: AMD clinches second mega chip supply deal, this time with Meta
AMD secures Meta as next big AI chip customer

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So it's a situation with both a rosy outlook and critical risks. In that case, how should we interpret today's stock surge of over 8 percent?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: The market is showing clear signs of overheating right now. It seems market participants have entered a state of greed, captivated by sensational headlines like '$100 billion' and 'massive deal.' Today's stock surge appears to have priced in only the best-case scenario, completely ignoring the negative factors we just discussed, like customer concentration risk, supply chain risk, and potential shareholder dilution. Therefore, there are concerns that the current stock price is closer to an irrational exuberance over short-term good news, rather than a balanced assessment of the company's intrinsic value and risks.

sources.title: AMD Just Won Another Massive AI Chip Deal. Its Stock Is Soaring.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Let's wrap up today's market action and then touch on the key economic indicators we should be watching.

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Today, the market finished mixed as hopes for the end of the Fed's rate-hiking cycle coexisted with inflation concerns. We're seeing investors react more sensitively to economic data releases as they try to gauge the future direction. Coming up tomorrow, we'll get a read on the labor market's temperature with the weekly initial jobless claims. Then, on Friday this week, the Producer Price Index (PPI) will be released. These two indicators will be critical turning points that will set the market's short-term tone.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: The Producer Price Index, or PPI, is often seen as a leading indicator for the Consumer Price Index (CPI). What should we be watching for in this upcoming release?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: That's right. Since PPI reflects production costs for businesses, it's a key leading indicator for final consumer prices. Last month's core PPI came in hotter than expected at 0.7%, which raised inflation alarms. This time, the consensus forecast is for a more moderate 0.3%. If the number meets or comes in below expectations, it could reinforce confidence in the disinflationary trend. But if it once again surprises to the upside, concerns about the Fed's 'higher for longer' stance could pressure the market again.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: And looking past this week into early March, there are even more significant indicators on the horizon that could really shift the market's direction, right?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Absolutely. In the first week of March, we'll get the ISM Manufacturing PMI, which gives us a gauge of the manufacturing sector's health. But the main event will undoubtedly be the jobs report on March 6th. The change in non-farm payrolls and the unemployment rate are among the most critical data points for the Fed. The market's expectations for the Fed's next move will largely depend on whether last month's slowdown in job growth, which was just 130,000, continues or if the labor market shows renewed strength. An overheating job market needs to cool down for inflationary pressures to ease.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: So we have a string of really crucial economic data releases coming up. To close, what's the key takeaway for investors?

scripts.speaker: 해설자
scripts.text: Looking ahead, the market is likely to remain data-dependent, moving more in response to macroeconomic indicators than to individual company earnings. Rather than getting caught up in short-term volatility, it will be wise to calmly assess whether the incoming data aligns with the bigger picture of disinflation and a soft landing for the economy. It'll be particularly important to watch the trends in employment and inflation data to anticipate the tone of Fed officials' comments leading up to the next FOMC meeting.

scripts.speaker: 진행자
scripts.text: Alright, thank you for that detailed analysis and outlook. That concludes our market closing brief for February 25th. Thanks for listening.
